Note some sites are located on the fault outside of the hazard area of interest but are used to inform fault activity on continuing into the area of interest.
field_definitions_raw: 1. FaultID: draft fault identification number.
2. FaultName: fault name.
3. CountryTer: For onshore faults, country or territory where the fault is located. ‘Offshore’ is used for faults that do not have a section on land. PR–Puerto Rico, HIS–Hispaniola.
4. FaultDip: dip (degrees). Default values are 90° dip for strike-slip faults, 50° dip for normal faults, and 60° dip for thrust faults. Uncertainties are considered during implementation.
5. DipDir: azimuthal direction of primary dip direction. ‘Vertical’ is listed for faults with a 90° dip.
6. Rake: rake (degrees) following Aki and Richards (1980) convention (normal = -90°; right-lateral = 180°; left-lateral = 0°; reverse = 90°).
7. UpDep: upper seismogenic depth (km).
8. LowerDep: lower seismogenic depth (km).

1. FaultID: fault or polygon ID for fault sections; this value links the EQGeoDB to the current fault section and fault polygon datasets. Note some sites are located on the fault outside of the hazard area of interest but are used to inform fault activity on continuing into the area of interest.
2. SiteID: site ID unique to each point geometry.
3. CountryTer: For onshore faults, country or territory where the fault is located. ‘Offshore’ is used for faults that do not have a section on land. PR–Puerto Rico, HIS–Hispaniola.
4. FaultName: fault name.
5. SiteName: name of site where slip rate or paleoseismic observations and/or measurements were made.
6. DataType: data type describing style of rate. Options are Slip rate study, Earthquake recurrence, Categorical slip rate, or PaleoseismicTrenchObs.
7. Obsern: observations used to derive slip rate, paleoseismic trench, or paleoliquefaction features as reported in the Reference field. See .csv file for complete descriptions.
8. NumEvents: number of reported events that are used to calculate a given slip rate or recurrence interval.
9. EvntTiming: author-defined age(s) of paleoearthquake event(s), in ka.
10. PeriodComp: time period over which paleoseismic observations are considered complete (i.e., no missing events), in years.
11. Recurrence: recurrence interval calculated using EvntTiming and NumEvents fields, in kiloyears.
12. RecurUn: uncertainty of recurrence interval as reported (i.e., maximum and minimum bounds on the recurrence interval), in kiloyears.

13. RepRint: distinction between whether the rates reported here are as reported/defined by the original source (Reported), or if original data has been reinterpreted internally (Reinterpreted). If the latter, notes in this cell reflect how calculations are performed.
14. OffType: basic description of offset measurement.
15. Offset_m: magnitude of offset, in meters.
16. Age_ka: age of feature offset, in thousands of years (ka).

17. AgeType: dating technique to determine age of offset features. Options are: OSL (optically stimulated luminescence), 14C (radiocarbon), K-Ar (potassium-argon) or estimated (age not determined radiometrically and is estimated from regional stratigraphic or geomorphic relationships).
18. SlipRteInt: type of slip rate. Options include open-ended (including an open or minimum time interval to the past and/or present) and closed (calculated using paleoearthquake timing information).
19. RateAge_ka: time interval over which rate is valid (in ka).

20. PrefRate: reported preferred rate if listed for a slip rate study. If not listed in original citation, but this field has a value, this is an average (mid-point) value between reported/reinterpreted min and max slip rate values (mm/yr).
21. LowRate: lower boundary of rate (mm/yr).
22. HighRate: upper boundary of rate (mm/yr).
23. RateType: slip rate type. Options are unprojected (vertical), projected (dip slip), or horizontal.
24. QbinMin: lower boundary of categorical slip rate bin (mm/yr).
25. QbinMax: upper boundary of categorical slip rate bin (mm/yr).
26. Reference: reference(s) used to compile this rate or recurrence information.
27. X: latitude of site (Decimal Degrees, WGS84).
28. Y: longitude of site (Decimal Degrees, WGS84).

rows_raw.detailed notes: Fault-zone polygon added based on new geomorphic mapping in Mann et al. (2005a) and Thompson Jobe et al. (in press) that document probable tectonic scarps and lateral offsets, near-shore seismic reflection data in Grindlay et al., 2005 that document likely Holocene faulting, paleoliquefaction features in the Anasco and Culebrinas valleys described in Tuttle et al., 2005 that suggest the Cerro Goden is the most likely fault source. Due to uncertainty in fault location onshore (away from mountain front, as described in Mann et al., 2005a, or at mountain front, as described in Thompson Jobe et al., in prep), a fault-zone polygon with a proxy fault is used.
